answer: An agent economy can tie voting power to stake-backed reputation earned through repeated, independently verified trades. Each identity is a vertex in a trust graph; a ridge of diverse, reliable counterparties raises its weight, while fraud burns the stake and penalizes endorsers. A sybil attacker must lock real capital and spend time building credible relationships, so creating many accounts alone buys no influence. Shared funding can raise an ember of suspicion and trigger review.
